item.title: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
item.description:
No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. item.title: Zack Polanski backs report endorsing Nato membership and maintaining nuclear weapons
item.description:
Russia warned Monday that it could carry out a "preventive nuclear attack" under certain circumstances, with former President Dmitry Medvedev claiming Ukraine and NATO allies have already crossed certain thresholds that could push Moscow to consider using nuclear weapons. "The massive use of non-nuclear means that cause catastrophes makes a preventive nuclear attack by the Russian Federation possible," Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council , wrote in an article published Monday in the Moscow Journal of International Law and excerpted by the state news agency TASS . Medvedev also warned that "secret or hidden supplies of nuclear weapons from the West to Kyiv will provoke a legitimate preventive nuclear attack by Russia." item.title: As the real world falls apart, Grand Theft Auto looks more and more appealing | Dave Schilling
item.description:
While I've already written about some of the wider political conversations (and that's a generous use of that word) when it comes to Grand Theft Auto VI , a smaller but maybe more topical one--since it hits closer to home for the kind of person reading this website--has been the debate about what GTA VI means to someone who both enjoys good video games but also supports the rights of the people who make them. Consider, when surveying not just the game that it ended up being, but the work that went into making it, that multiple things can be true about Grand Theft Auto VI at once. Like: It is a staggering achievement of scale, fidelity, technical prowess and human creativity. The studio responsible for the game stands accused of union-busting, throwing people who spent years making the game into the bin during one of the worst climates for games employment in the industry's history .…

item.title: Thousands flee Manchester concert after unknown substance released
item.description:

item.title: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
item.description:
Students wait for the start of the annual college entrance exams at an exam hall in Seoul on Nov. 19, 2026. —Kim Hong-Ji—Pool/AFP/Getty Images South Korea’s education minister has resigned after intense backlash against new rules meant to prevent cheating using artificial intelligence during the country’s high-stakes college entrance exams. Choi Kyo-jin announced his resignation on Sunday in response to “criticism or blame from the public for failing to prepare adequately in advance.” The Ministry of Education had announced the new exam measures on Tuesday, just two days before nearly 500,000 South Koreans took the hourslong College Scholastic Ability Test, also called Suneung . Under the new rules, test-takers were required to have their glasses inspected, cover their shirt buttons to prevent the use of cameras, and roll up their sleeves. item.title: NATO witnesses a surge of airspace violations by Russia as Moscow seeks to test alliance
item.description:
The Polish army secures a suspected impact site of a Russian projectile in July 2026. AFP via Getty Images NATO convened an urgent meeting on Nov. 23, 2026 , to discuss the violation of members’ airspace by Russia. It follows an incident three days earlier in which three objects – believed to be two missiles and a drone – crashed in Poland in what the country’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, described as an “intentional provocation” by Russia . If true, it would be far from the first such testing of the airspace of a NATO country. Russian aircraft, drones and missiles have violated NATO airspace dozens of times since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. And while individually, many of these incidents appear minor – a drone crash here, a brief fighter incursion there, a missile discovered only after the fact – taken together, I believe the numbers tell a far more…

item.title: Fourth Circuit Upholds Virginia's Law Terminating Agreements to Help With Immigration Enforcement - but Strikes Down anti-Mask Law
item.description:
Flag of Virginia (Wellesenterprises/Dreamstime.com) In September, I wrote about the the federal district court decision striking down Virginia's new law terminating Section 287(g) agreements, under which various state and local law enforcement agencies agree to help with federal immigration enforcement. Today, in United States v. Virginia , the US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit reversed that decision. But, at the same time, in a 2-1 ruling, they struck down Virginia's law barring law enforcement officers (including federal ones) from wearing masks except in relatively narrowly specified circumstances. item.title: Butt of the joke: Trump impersonator mocks president at Canada press dinner
item.description:
Carney watches on as comedian lampoons US leader and his interest in men’s backsides at correspondents’ event Ottawa Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday. With coiffed hair and an ill-fitting suit, comedian Mark Critch – who portrays the president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes – danced on to the stage and lampooned the trade war Trump started as well as the president’s threats to annex Canada.
